A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 22-page versions of PhySense, including Appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of their equations, figures, tables and narrative.

before.justification: v4 reports original reconstruction and sensor-placement experiments on turbulent flow, sea temperature and simulated car aerodynamics, with additional empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, ablations and statistical analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The flow-matching reconstructor, cross-attention conditioning, DiT/Transolver backbones and projected-gradient sensor-placement optimization remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Coverage remains turbulent flow, global sea surface temperature with land constraints, and car-surface pressure on a 3D irregular mesh. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: SSPOR, VoronoiCNN, Senseiver, S3GM and DiffusionPDE retain their benchmark-specific participation, and the placement comparators are unchanged. The newly cited Marcato et al. work is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–D retain the same data splits, sensor counts, training budgets, model configurations and evaluation procedures, including relative L2 error and gradient-field evaluation.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix D retain the same incorporation and noise-input ablations, placement generalization tests, initialization and learning-rate sensitivity analyses, and attention and placement visualizations.

E5.justification: Appendix D.3 still reports training the base model once and repeating reconstruction three times, with means and standard deviations in Tables 14–15. Appendix D.5 retains the same three-initialization sample-mean and sample-variance analysis.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings match throughout, including Tables 2–7 and 12–16. For example, Table 3 retains 15-sensor car errors of 0.0465 for PhySense and 0.0386 for PhySense-opt.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1 and 3.5, the conditional Gaussian assumption, optimality definitions and bounds, and all Appendix A proofs and derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same two-stage framework, variance-minimization guarantees, state-of-the-art performance claims and claimed discovery of informative sensor placements.

C2.justification: Interpretations of reconstruction quality, placement generalization, efficiency and uncertainty are unchanged. Appendix E retains the limitation that point-wise observations do not represent sensors that integrate information over spatial regions.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical hardware, software, hyperparameters, simulation details and optimization instructions. The code-access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds Marcato et al. (2024), 'Journey over destination: dynamic sensor placement enhances generalization,' as reference 33 and cites it in Section 2.2's existing placement-optimization discussion. All earlier cited works are retained; research positioning is otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: An additional citation marker, subsequent citation renumbering and the updated arXiv version/date stamp constitute limited editorial changes. Prose wording, terminology, headings and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added bibliography entry causes local reflow on pages 12–13, moving the Rudy et al. reference to page 13. Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–16 retain their structure and placement.

improvement.justification: Adding the Marcato et al. citation in Section 2.2 modestly improves acknowledgment of relevant prior sensor-placement research. This is a limited gain in scholarly completeness; the scientific evidence, theoretical support and substantive exposition remain unchanged.
